# Converting from JABBA and SPiCT

## JABBA: `jbinput2jabba3()`

`jbinput2jabba3()` takes the object returned by `JABBA::build_jabba()`, or a
fitted `JABBA::fit_jabba()` object, and returns `list(data, priors, model)` for
`jabba3()`. It carries over the priors (r, K, psi to `bkinit`, shape,
catchability, status priors), the production lag, catch error, catchability and
variance groups, `proc.dev.all`, the BioProcDyn process-error options, auxiliary
data and the Selex curves, and reports each difference:

- the observation error is carried over exactly: the index se are JABBA's total
  input SD, `sqrt(SE2)` (se and `fixed.obsE` combined), with `se.min = 0`;
- JABBA's gamma(a, b) prior on the inverse process variance
  (`build_jabba(igamma = )`, default c(4, 0.01)) is kept exactly when it is
  informative (`jb3_priors(sdb = "igamma", igamma = c(a, b))`); the diffuse
  inverse-gamma(0.001, 0.001) can collapse to sdb = 0 at the posterior mode and
  is replaced by a proxy (`igamma.proxy`): the JABBA posterior of sigma.proc as a
  lognormal prior on sdb (`"posterior"`, the default for a fit) or sdb fixed at
  its posterior median (`"fixed"`), and the FishLife prior for a `build_jabba()`
  object (`"fishlife"`); `"igamma"` keeps it (for `engine = "nuts"`);
- q gets a flat prior on log q (`q.uniform = TRUE` reproduces the JAGS uniform
  prior on q);
- JABBA reports posterior medians, JABBA3 the posterior mode (unless
  `engine = "nuts"`).

For a fit, the JABBA trajectories are returned in `x$jabba$ts` (same format as
`fit$ts`) for a direct comparison:

```{r conv-jabbafit, eval = FALSE}
jbfit <- JABBA::fit_jabba(jb, ni = 30000, nt = 5, nb = 10000, nc = 2)   # JAGS
x  <- jbinput2jabba3(jbfit)                # data, priors and settings of the fit
f3 <- jabba3(x$data, x$priors, x$model)
merge(f3$ts[f3$ts$quant == "B/Bmsy", c("year", "est")],
      x$jabba$ts[x$jabba$ts$quant == "B/Bmsy", c("year", "est")], by = "year", suffixes = c(".jabba3", ".jabba"))
```

> ICCAT bigeye, JABBA Fox model in JAGS (sigma.est = FALSE, fixed.obsE = 0.01): with
> JABBA's default inverse-gamma(4, 0.01) carried over exactly, the JABBA3 $B/B_{MSY}$ and
> $F/F_{MSY}$ are within 2% of the JABBA medians in every year (K 1.21 vs 1.23 million t);
> with the diffuse inverse-gamma(0.001, 0.001) and the posterior proxy within 4%, and with
> sdb fixed at the posterior median within 3%.

```{r conv-jabba, eval = requireNamespace("JABBA", quietly = TRUE)}
jb <- JABBA::build_jabba(catch = bet$catch, cpue = bet$cpue, se = bet$se, model.type = "Fox",
                         r.prior = c(0.2, 0.5), psi.prior = c(0.9, 0.25), verbose = FALSE)
options(scipen = 0)          # build_jabba() sets options(scipen = 999)
x  <- jbinput2jabba3(jb)
f2 <- jabba3(x$data, x$priors, x$model, osa = FALSE)
signif(f2$pars[c("K", "r", "sdb"), c("est", "lci", "uci")], 4)
```

> With JABBA's default inverse-gamma(4, 0.01) process-error prior carried over, K =
> 1.21 million t and $B/B_{MSY}$ = 0.74 in 2017 (the JABBA3 FishLife prior gives K = 1,174,749
> and 0.797, chapter *JABBA-like or SPiCT-like*).

## SPiCT: `spictinp2jabba3()`

`spictinp2jabba3()` takes a SPiCT input list (`inp`, as passed to
`spict::fit.spict()`). JABBA3 is an annual model: catches are summed by
calendar year and several index observations in a year are averaged
(geometric mean). The model years span the catch and the indices, as in SPiCT;
the catch in index years without catch is estimated with the hybrid F random
walk (see the thornback ray chapter). SPiCT's observation-error form is used
(`obs.error = "spict"`): the observation SD is `sdi[index] * stdevfacI`, and
the catch SD `sdc * stdevfacC`. The priors `logr`, `logK`, `logbkfrac`,
`logsdb`, `logn`, `logsdi` (one prior per index when given by index) and
`logsdf` carry over with their on/off switches, a fixed `n` (phase -1)
fixes the shape, and `logngamma` becomes a lognormal prior on m. By default
(`spict.like = TRUE`) the conversion keeps SPiCT's process structure: a random
walk on F in all years (`frw = "all"`), which is how SPiCT identifies the scale
when the catch is known; the catch SD estimated when SPiCT has a `logsdc` prior;
no K prior unless SPiCT has one, no cap on K, and the best of several starting
values (including K-profile starts); `jabba3()` warns when K exceeds the
r-based plausibility bound. `spict.like = FALSE` gives the catch-conditioned
(JABBA-like) conversion. The `alpha` and `beta` priors (ratios of observation
to process SDs) have no JABBA3 equivalent and are reported as dropped. Chapter
*JABBA-like or SPiCT-like* explains the settings and shows the manual set-up;
the thornback ray chapter converts a full ICES benchmark assessment.

A SPiCT-style input list built from the bigeye data:

```{r conv-spict}
ok1 <- is.finite(bet$cpue[, 2]); ok2 <- is.finite(bet$cpue[, 3])
inp <- list(obsC = bet$catch[, 2], timeC = bet$catch[, 1],
            obsI = list(bet$cpue[ok1, 2], bet$cpue[ok2, 3]),
            timeI = list(bet$cpue[ok1, 1] + 0.5, bet$cpue[ok2, 1] + 0.5),
            priors = list(logr = c(log(0.2), 0.5, 1), logn = c(log(2), 2, 0), logbkfrac = c(log(0.8), 0.5, 1)),
            ini = list(logn = log(2)), phases = list(logn = -1))
xs <- spictinp2jabba3(inp, stock = "bet")
fs <- jabba3(xs$data, xs$priors, xs$model, osa = FALSE)
signif(fs$pars[c("K", "r", "sdb"), c("est", "lci", "uci")], 4)
```

With the spict package installed, its example data convert the same way:

```{r conv-spict-pol, eval = requireNamespace("spict", quietly = TRUE)}
data(pol, package = "spict")
xp <- spictinp2jabba3(pol$albacore, stock = "albacore")
fp <- jabba3(xp$data, xp$priors, xp$model)
fp
```
